source.text: חֲזוֹן֙ יְשַֽׁעְיָ֣הוּ בֶן־אָמ֔וֹץ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָזָ֔ה עַל־יְהוּדָ֖ה וִירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם בִּימֵ֨י עֻזִּיָּ֧הוּ יוֹתָ֛ם אָחָ֥ז יְחִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ מַלְכֵ֥י יְהוּדָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] vision of Isaiah son of Amoz, which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem in [the] days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, Hezekiah, kings of Judah.

en.L: The vision of Isaiah son of Amoz, which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, [and] Hezekiah, kings of Judah.
en.B: The vision of Isaiah son of Amoz: what he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem in the days when Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah were kings of Judah.
en.R: Isaiah son of Amoz saw these things in visions from God. They were about Judah and its capital city, Jerusalem. He saw them while Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah were kings of Judah.

es.L: Visión de Isaías hijo de Amoz, que vio acerca de Judá y Jerusalén en los días de Uzías, Jotam, Acaz [y] Ezequías, reyes de Judá.
es.B: La visión de Isaías hijo de Amoz: lo que vio acerca de Judá y de Jerusalén en los días en que Uzías, Jotam, Acaz y Ezequías eran reyes de Judá.
es.R: Isaías hijo de Amoz vio estas cosas en visiones que Dios le dio. Trataban sobre Judá y su capital, Jerusalén. Las vio cuando Uzías, Jotam, Acaz y Ezequías eran reyes de Judá.

fr.L: La vision d’Isaïe fils d’Amots, qu’il vit au sujet de Juda et de Jérusalem aux jours d’Ozias, de Jotham, d’Achaz [et] d’Ézéchias, rois de Juda.
fr.B: La vision d’Isaïe fils d’Amots : ce qu’il vit au sujet de Juda et de Jérusalem au temps où Ozias, Jotham, Achaz et Ézéchias étaient rois de Juda.
fr.R: Isaïe fils d’Amots a vu ces choses dans des visions venues de Dieu. Elles concernaient Juda et sa capitale, Jérusalem. Il les a vues pendant que Ozias, Jotham, Achaz et Ézéchias étaient rois de Juda.

sw.L: Maono ya Isaya mwana wa Amozi, aliyoyaona kuhusu Yuda na Yerusalemu katika siku za Uzia, Yothamu, Ahazi, [na] Hezekia, wafalme wa Yuda.
sw.B: Maono ya Isaya mwana wa Amozi: yale aliyoyaona kuhusu Yuda na Yerusalemu katika siku ambazo Uzia, Yothamu, Ahazi na Hezekia walikuwa wafalme wa Yuda.
sw.R: Isaya mwana wa Amozi aliona mambo haya katika maono kutoka kwa Mungu. Yalihusu Yuda na mji wake mkuu, Yerusalemu. Aliyaona wakati Uzia, Yothamu, Ahazi na Hezekia walipokuwa wafalme wa Yuda.

vi.L: Khải tượng của Ê-sai con trai A-mốt, điều ông đã thấy về Giu-đa và Giê-ru-sa-lem trong những ngày của Ô-xia, Giô-tham, A-cha, [và] Ê-xê-chia, các vua Giu-đa.
vi.B: Khải tượng của Ê-sai con trai A-mốt: những điều ông đã thấy về Giu-đa và Giê-ru-sa-lem trong thời Ô-xia, Giô-tham, A-cha và Ê-xê-chia làm vua Giu-đa.
vi.R: Ê-sai con trai A-mốt đã thấy những điều này trong các khải tượng Đức Chúa Trời ban cho ông. Những điều ấy nói về Giu-đa và kinh đô của Giu-đa là Giê-ru-sa-lem. Ông thấy những điều ấy trong thời Ô-xia, Giô-tham, A-cha và Ê-xê-chia làm vua Giu-đa.

ko.L: 아모스의 아들 이사야의 환상, 곧 그가 유다 왕들인 웃시야와 요담과 아하스와 히스기야의 시대에 유다와 예루살렘에 관하여 본 것이다.
ko.B: 아모스의 아들 이사야가 받은 환상이다. 이것은 웃시야와 요담과 아하스와 히스기야가 유다를 다스리던 때에 그가 유다와 예루살렘에 관하여 본 것이다.
ko.R: 아모스의 아들 이사야는 하나님께서 보여 주신 환상으로 이 일들을 보았다. 그것은 유다와 그 수도 예루살렘에 관한 것이었다. 그가 이것을 본 것은 웃시야와 요담과 아하스와 히스기야가 유다의 왕이었을 때였다.

pt.L: A visão de Isaías, filho de Amoz, que ele viu acerca de Judá e de Jerusalém nos dias de Uzias, Jotão, Acaz [e] Ezequias, reis de Judá.
pt.B: A visão de Isaías, filho de Amoz: o que ele viu a respeito de Judá e de Jerusalém no tempo em que Uzias, Jotão, Acaz e Ezequias foram reis de Judá.
pt.R: Isaías, filho de Amoz, viu estas coisas em visões que vieram de Deus. Elas falavam de Judá e da sua capital, Jerusalém. Isaías as viu no tempo em que Uzias, Jotão, Acaz e Ezequias eram reis de Judá.

am.L: የአሞጽ ልጅ የኢሳይያስ ራእይ፤ [ይህም] በይሁዳ ነገሥታት በዖዝያ፣ በኢዮአታም፣ በአካዝና በሕዝቅያስ ዘመን ስለ ይሁዳና ስለ ኢየሩሳሌም ያየው [ነው]።
am.B: የአሞጽ ልጅ የኢሳይያስ ራእይ፤ ዖዝያ፣ ኢዮአታም፣ አካዝና ሕዝቅያስ በይሁዳ ላይ በነገሡበት ዘመን ስለ ይሁዳና ስለ ኢየሩሳሌም ያየው ይህ ነው።
am.R: የአሞጽ ልጅ ኢሳይያስ እነዚህን ነገሮች እግዚአብሔር ባሳየው ራእይ አየ። ነገሮቹ ስለ ይሁዳና ስለ ዋና ከተማዋ ስለ ኢየሩሳሌም ነበሩ። ኢሳይያስ ያያቸው ዖዝያ፣ ኢዮአታም፣ አካዝና ሕዝቅያስ የይሁዳ ነገሥታት በነበሩበት ጊዜ ነው።

hi.L: आमोस के पुत्र यशायाह का दर्शन, जो उसने यहूदा और यरूशलेम के विषय में यहूदा के राजाओं उज्जियाह, योताम, आहाज़ [और] हिजकिय्याह के दिनों में देखा।
hi.B: आमोस के पुत्र यशायाह का दर्शन: वह जो उसने यहूदा और यरूशलेम के विषय में उन दिनों में देखा जब उज्जियाह, योताम, आहाज़ और हिजकिय्याह यहूदा के राजा थे।
hi.R: आमोस के बेटे यशायाह ने परमेश्वर से मिले दर्शनों में ये बातें देखीं। ये बातें यहूदा और उसकी राजधानी यरूशलेम के बारे में थीं। उसने इन्हें उस समय देखा जब उज्जियाह, योताम, आहाज़ और हिजकिय्याह यहूदा के राजा थे।

ru.L: Видение Исаии, сына Амоса, которое он видел об Иуде и Иерусалиме во дни Озии, Иоафама, Ахаза [и] Езекии, царей Иудейских.
ru.B: Видение Исаии, сына Амоса: то, что он увидел об Иуде и Иерусалиме в те дни, когда царями Иуды были Озия, Иоафам, Ахаз и Езекия.
ru.R: Исаия, сын Амоса, видел это в видениях от Бога. Они были об Иуде и о его столице, Иерусалиме. Он видел их, когда царями Иуды были Озия, Иоафам, Ахаз и Езекия.

ja.L: アモツの子イザヤの幻。これは、ユダの王ウジヤ、ヨタム、アハズ、ヒゼキヤの日々に、彼がユダとエルサレムについて見たものである。
ja.B: アモツの子イザヤの幻。ウジヤ、ヨタム、アハズ、ヒゼキヤがユダの王であった時代に、イザヤがユダとエルサレムについて見たもの。
ja.R: アモツの息子イザヤは、神から幻を示されて、これらのことを見ました。それは、ユダと、その都エルサレムについてのことでした。イザヤがこれを見たのは、ウジヤ、ヨタム、アハズ、ヒゼキヤがユダの王だったころです。

decisions.choice: vision: what God showed the prophet, his message as a whole
decisions.reason: The noun and the verb "he saw" come from the same root. A "vision" here is not one dream or sight but the whole message God revealed to Isaiah, and the verse is the title of the book (compare Obadiah 1; Nahum 1:1; 2 Chronicles 32:32, which speaks of "the vision of Isaiah").

decisions.choice: Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, Hezekiah: kings of Judah in the second half of the eighth century BC
decisions.reason: Isaiah's call came in the year King Uzziah died (6:1). He spoke to Ahaz during the Syrian and Israelite threat (chapter 7) and to Hezekiah during the Assyrian invasion of 701 BC (chapters 36-39). The book thus covers some forty years or more of his work (2 Kings 15-20).

decisions.choice: saw these things in visions from God ... its capital city
decisions.reason: Readable says where the vision came from and explains that Jerusalem was Judah's capital. Both are clear from the book itself.

decisions.choice: "Maono" for the vision (hazon)
decisions.reason: The plural "maono" is the usual Swahili word for what a prophet sees, and here it names the whole message of the book (m1). The names keep the forms of 2 Kings and 2 Chronicles: Isaya mwana wa Amozi, Uzia, Yothamu, Ahazi, Hezekia.

decisions.choice: "Isaïe fils d’Amots"
decisions.reason: The prophet’s name keeps the form of every published French verse (Matthew 3:3; 2 Kings 19:2), for the whole book; data/books.json has "Ésaïe" as the book title, a question left for the reviewer.

decisions.choice: "qu’il vit" (L, B); "il a vu" (R)
decisions.reason: The title is narration: passé simple at Literal and Balanced, passé composé at Readable. The oracles that follow are speech and use the present, future and passé composé at every level, for the whole book; the prophet’s and God’s words take no quotation marks.

decisions.choice: "khải tượng" (vision)
decisions.reason: "Khải tượng" is the established word for a prophet's God-given vision and covers the whole message, as the meaning decision reads it; the older "sự hiện thấy" sounds archaic.

decisions.choice: "환상" for the vision (*ḥazon*) that names the book
decisions.reason: "환상" is the common word for what a prophet is shown; "묵시" is the older church word and now suggests apocalyptic writing.

decisions.choice: "아모스의 아들 이사야"
decisions.reason: The terms note's published form (2 Kings 19:2); Korean Protestant tradition spells Isaiah's father like the prophet Amos, though the Hebrew names differ.

decisions.choice: A visão de Isaías, filho de Amoz (L, B); Isaías, filho de Amoz, viu ... em visões (R); Uzias, Jotão, Acaz, Ezequias
decisions.reason: For the whole book: the title keeps the noun "visão" (m1) at Literal and Balanced, the word a Portuguese reader knows for a prophet's message from God; Readable turns it into a sentence, as the English Readable does. The prophet is "Isaías, filho de Amoz" with commas, as 2 Kings 19:2 and 20:1 name him in Portuguese, and the four kings take the forms 2 Kings 15-20 gives them: "Uzias", "Jotão", "Acaz", "Ezequias". Later headings in the book (2:1 and the oracles of 13-23) use the same plain heading style.

decisions.choice: names as in 2 Kings 15-20 and 2 Chronicles 26-32 on main: Isaiah son of Amoz "የአሞጽ ልጅ ኢሳይያስ", Uzziah "ዖዝያ", Jotham "ኢዮአታም", Ahaz "አካዝ", Hezekiah "ሕዝቅያስ"; vision "ራእይ"
decisions.reason: The kings and the prophet are the same people as in the histories, so their names keep the forms already used there (Uzziah as 2 Kings 15:13). "ራእይ" is the word for what God shows a prophet and is used for the whole book, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: the oracles are set in lines at every level, with a \q break wherever the English level has one; God's own words are given without quotation marks where the English has none
decisions.reason: Isaiah is mostly Hebrew poetry spoken by the prophet in God's name. One Amharic line is kept for each English line, the verb at the end of its own line where the clause allows. Speech marks follow the English of each level, so the record counts the same quotations in every language.

decisions.choice: यशायाह, आमोस; उज्जियाह, योताम, आहाज़, हिजकिय्याह
decisions.reason: The prophet and the four kings keep the forms 2 Kings 15-20 already uses in this translation (आमोस के पुत्र यशायाह, 2 Kings 19:2; उज्जियाह, योताम, आहाज़, हिजकिय्याह), and यशायाह is the New Testament's form (Matthew 13:14). Book-wide choice for Isaiah.

decisions.choice: "Исаия, сын Амоса"; the kings "Озия, Иоафам, Ахаз, Езекия"
decisions.reason: The names keep the forms already used in this translation: Isaiah as in the New Testament and 2 Kings 19:2, Amoz as in 2 Kings 19:2, and the four kings as in 2 Kings 15-20 and 2 Chronicles 26-32. Judah is "Иуда" (the tribe and kingdom), as in Kings, not "Иудея".

decisions.choice: Book-wide register for Isaiah (and the prophets after it): the oracles in verse are plain style (だ・である) at every level, Readable too, by the OT poetry rule; God speaks of himself as "わたし" and his acts in the third person take light respect forms (語られた, 言われる). Prose (this superscription, 2:1, the narratives of chapters 6-8, 20, 36-39) follows the narrative rule: plain at Literal and Balanced, です・ます at Readable. hazon is "幻" at every level.
alternatives: です・ます at Readable throughout the book
decisions.reason: The English sets the oracles as poetry and the superscription as prose; OT_SUPPLEMENT gives plain style for verse at every level and the narrative register for prose, as in 2 Samuel 22 inside 2 Samuel. "幻" is the ordinary word for what a prophet is shown and keeps the link with chazah "saw".

decisions.choice: Names as in 2 Kings and 2 Chronicles: "アモツの子イザヤ" (L, B), "アモツの息子イザヤ" (R); the kings "ウジヤ", "ヨタム", "アハズ", "ヒゼキヤ".
decisions.reason: The Hebrew here is Uzziyyahu, the form 2 Kings 15 and 2 Chronicles 26 give as ウジヤ; one form per person across the historical books and the prophets.

source.text: שִׁמְע֤וּ שָׁמַ֨יִם֙ וְהַאֲזִ֣ינִי אֶ֔רֶץ כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבֵּ֑ר בָּנִים֙ גִּדַּ֣לְתִּי וְרוֹמַ֔מְתִּי וְהֵ֖ם פָּ֥שְׁעוּ בִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Hear, heavens, and give ear, earth, for Yahweh has spoken: children I have raised and brought up, and they have rebelled against me.

en.L: Hear, O heavens, and give ear, O earth, \q for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken: \q Children I have reared and brought up, \q and they have rebelled against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: Listen, heavens; earth, open your ears, \q for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken: \q I raised children and made them great, \q but they have rebelled against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: Sky, listen! Earth, listen! {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken. He says: \q I raised children and helped them grow up. \q But they have turned against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

es.L: {{plural_you:Oigan|Oíd}}, cielos, y presta oído, tierra, \q porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha hablado: \q Hijos he criado y engrandecido, \q y ellos se han rebelado contra {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.
es.B: {{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}}, cielos; tierra, abre tus oídos, \q porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha hablado: \q Crié hijos y los hice crecer, \q pero ellos se han rebelado contra {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.
es.R: ¡Cielo, escucha! ¡Tierra, escucha! {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha hablado. Él dice: \q Crié hijos y los ayudé a crecer. \q Pero ellos se han puesto en contra de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.

fr.L: Écoutez, cieux, et prête l’oreille, terre, \q car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a parlé : \q J’ai élevé des fils et je les ai fait grandir, \q et ils se sont révoltés contre {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.
fr.B: Écoutez, cieux ; terre, tends l’oreille, \q car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a parlé : \q J’ai élevé des enfants, je les ai fait grandir, \q mais ils se sont révoltés contre {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.
fr.R: Ciel, écoute ! Terre, écoute ! {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a parlé. Il dit : \q J’ai élevé des enfants et je les ai aidés à grandir. \q Mais ils se sont tournés contre {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.

sw.L: Sikieni, enyi mbingu, nawe, dunia, tega sikio, \q kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amenena: \q Wana nimewalea na kuwakuza, \q nao wameniasi {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}.
sw.B: Sikilizeni, enyi mbingu; dunia, tega masikio yako, \q kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amesema: \q Nimewalea watoto na kuwafanya wakubwa, \q lakini wameniasi.
sw.R: Anga, sikiliza! Dunia, sikiliza! {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amesema. Anasema hivi: \q Niliwalea watoto na kuwasaidia wakue. \q Lakini wamegeuka dhidi {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}.

vi.L: Hỡi các tầng trời, hãy nghe; hỡi đất, hãy lắng tai, \q vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã phán: \q Ta đã nuôi nấng và dưỡng dục con cái, \q mà chúng đã phản nghịch {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.B: Hỡi trời, hãy nghe; hỡi đất, hãy lắng tai, \q vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã phán: \q Ta đã nuôi con cái khôn lớn, \q nhưng chúng đã phản nghịch {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.R: Hỡi bầu trời, hãy nghe! Hỡi đất, hãy nghe! {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã phán. Ngài phán: \q Ta đã nuôi con cái và giúp chúng khôn lớn. \q Nhưng chúng đã chống lại {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.

ko.L: 하늘아, 들어라. 땅아, 귀를 기울여라. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 말씀하셨다. \q 내가 자식들을 기르고 키웠는데, \q 그들이 나를 거역했다.
ko.B: 하늘아, 들어라. 땅아, 귀를 기울여라. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 말씀하신다. \q 내가 자식들을 기르고 크게 키웠으나, \q 그들이 나를 거역했다.
ko.R: 하늘아, 들어라! 땅아, 들어라! {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 말씀하신다. \q 나는 자식들을 기르고 자라게 했다. \q 그런데 그들은 나에게 등을 돌렸다.

pt.L: Ouçam, céus, e dá ouvidos, terra, \q porque {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} falou: \q Filhos eu criei e fiz crescer, \q e eles se rebelaram contra {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}.
pt.B: Ouçam, céus; terra, presta atenção, \q pois {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} falou: \q Eu criei filhos e os fiz crescer, \q mas eles se rebelaram contra {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}.
pt.R: Céus, escutem! Terra, escuta! {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} falou. Ele diz: \q Eu criei filhos e os ajudei a crescer. \q Mas eles se voltaram contra {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}}.

am.L: ሰማያት ሆይ፣ ስሙ፤ ምድር ሆይ፣ አድምጪ፤ \q {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ተናግሯልና፦ \q ልጆችን አሳደግኩ፤ ከፍም አደረግኋቸው፤ \q እነርሱም በእኔ ላይ ዓመፁ።
am.B: ሰማያት ሆይ፣ ስሙ፤ ምድር ሆይ፣ ጆሮሽን ስጪ፤ \q {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ተናግሯልና፦ \q ልጆችን አሳደግኩ፤ ታላቅም አደረግኋቸው፤ \q እነርሱ ግን በእኔ ላይ ዓመፁ።
am.R: ሰማይ ሆይ፣ ስማ! ምድር ሆይ፣ ስሚ! {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ተናግሯል። እንዲህ ይላል፦ \q ልጆችን አሳደግኩ፤ እንዲያድጉም ረዳኋቸው። \q እነርሱ ግን ከዱኝ።

hi.L: हे आकाश, सुनो, और हे पृथ्वी, कान लगाओ, \q क्योंकि {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} ने कहा है: \q मैंने बच्चों को पाला-पोसा और बड़ा किया, \q और उन्होंने मुझसे विद्रोह किया है।
hi.B: हे आकाश, सुनो; हे पृथ्वी, ध्यान से सुनो, \q क्योंकि {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} बोले हैं: \q मैंने बच्चों को पाला और उन्हें बड़ा बनाया, \q पर उन्होंने मेरे विरुद्ध विद्रोह किया है।
hi.R: हे आकाश, सुनो! हे पृथ्वी, सुनो! {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} ने कहा है। वे कहते हैं: \q मैंने बच्चों को पाला और बड़े होने में उनकी सहायता की। \q पर वे मेरे विरुद्ध हो गए हैं।

ru.L: Слушайте, небеса, и внимай, земля, \q потому что {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}} сказал: \q Детей {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} вскормил и вырастил, \q а они восстали против {{deity_pronoun:меня|Меня}}.
ru.B: Слушайте, небеса; земля, внимай, \q потому что {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}} сказал: \q Я растил детей и сделал их великими, \q а они восстали против {{deity_pronoun:меня|Меня}}.
ru.R: Небо, слушай! Земля, слушай! {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}} сказал. Он говорит: \q Я растил детей и помог им вырасти. \q А они восстали против {{deity_pronoun:меня|Меня}}.

ja.L: 天よ、聞け。地よ、耳を傾けよ。 \q {{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}が語られたのだから。 \q 子らをわたしは育て、大きくした。 \q だが彼らは、わたしに背いた。
ja.B: 天よ、聞きなさい。地よ、耳を傾けなさい。 \q {{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}が語られたのだ。 \q わたしは子らを育て、大きくした。 \q しかし彼らは、わたしに背いた。
ja.R: 天よ、聞きなさい！地よ、聞きなさい！{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}が語られたのだ。その方はこう言われる。 \q わたしは子どもたちを育て、大きくしてやった。 \q それなのに、彼らはわたしに背を向けた。

decisions.choice: hear, heavens ... give ear, earth: heaven and earth called as witnesses
decisions.reason: Moses called heaven and earth to witness the covenant and Israel's coming unfaithfulness (Deuteronomy 30:19; 31:28), and his song opens with the same two verbs (Deuteronomy 32:1). Isaiah begins as if in a court case: God brings a charge against his people, with all creation listening (compare Micah 6:1-2).

decisions.choice: rebelled: broken faith with their lord
decisions.reason: The verb is used of a subject people breaking away from their overlord (2 Kings 1:1; 8:20). Israel's sin is pictured as children rising against the father who raised them.

decisions.choice: God's words begin without a mark
decisions.reason: After "Yahweh has spoken" the voice changes to God's own "I" with no word such as "saying". The prophet's words and God's are woven together through the chapter.

decisions.choice: sky ... He says: ... helped them grow up
decisions.reason: Readable says "sky" for the heavens, adds "He says" to show that God is now speaking, and puts the two verbs of raising ("made great" and "lifted high") as "raised ... and helped them grow up".

decisions.choice: no quotation marks for God's speech in the oracles
decisions.reason: As in the English and the terms note for Isaiah, the prophet's words and God's first-person speech in the oracles take no quotation marks; only speech quoted inside an oracle takes « ». Book-wide choice, recorded here once for chapters 1-20.

decisions.choice: God's words follow "BWANA amenena:" with no quotation marks
decisions.reason: Book-wide in Isaiah: in the oracles the prophet's words and God's first-person speech take no quotation marks, and the formula is followed by a colon, as the English does (terms note). Speech quoted inside an oracle takes quotation marks.

decisions.choice: "des fils"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is "sons"; Literal keeps it, Balanced and Readable say "enfants" as the English says "children", since the whole people is meant.

decisions.choice: God speaking says "Ta"; no quotation marks around the oracle
decisions.reason: As the terms note settles for the whole book: God's first-person speech in the oracles is "Ta" (spanned mid-sentence) and, as in the English, takes no quotation marks; a "Ta" opening a line or sentence is written plainly with its capital.

decisions.choice: The prophet speaks of God with the honorific ("{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 말씀하셨다"); God's own words follow in the plain style (해라체) with "나", without quotation marks
decisions.reason: As in the terms note for Isaiah: the oracles take no quotation marks, and God never uses the honorific of himself. Korean has no capital letters, so the English deity_pronoun setting has no Korean span; respect for God is carried by "-시-" and "께서".

decisions.choice: "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}" for the divine name throughout Isaiah
decisions.reason: The Korean style guide's span: "주" by default, "야훼" with the setting; particles stay outside the span.

decisions.choice: Ouçam, céus (vocês); dá ouvidos / presta atenção / escuta, terra (tu)
decisions.reason: The heavens are called with a plural imperative and the earth with a singular one, as in Moses' song, which this verse echoes (m1). Portuguese keeps the same split Deuteronomy 32:1 makes in Portuguese: "vocês" forms for the heavens, "tu" for the earth.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans in Amharic
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the setting that capitalizes pronouns for God has nothing to change; the English spans on "me", "my" and "him" have no Amharic counterpart through the book.

decisions.choice: "ሰማያት ሆይ፣ ስሙ፤ ምድር ሆይ፣ አድምጪ" (L), "... ጆሮሽን ስጪ" (B); Readable "ሰማይ ሆይ፣ ስማ! ምድር ሆይ፣ ስሚ!"
decisions.reason: The call to heaven and earth as witnesses opens the book and is echoed in 1:10; the heavens are plural at Literal and Balanced and singular at Readable, as the style brief has it, and the earth is addressed as feminine, as Amharic usually treats ምድር in address.

decisions.choice: प्रभु for both YHWH and Adonai; the divine_name setting tells them apart
decisions.reason: Hindi प्रभु translates both the divine name YHWH and the title Adonai ("Lord"). Wherever the Hebrew has the name, प्रभु stands inside a divine_name span whose alternative is याहवे, so a reader who switches the setting sees which is which; where प्रभु stands alone it is Adonai. यहोवा (the Old Version's form) is not used. God takes honorific plural agreement (वे, बोले हैं) in both options.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Hindi
decisions.reason: The English marks God's pronouns ("me") with the deity_pronoun setting. Devanagari has no capital letters, so the Hindi has no such spans; respect for God is carried by the honorific third person (वे, उनका). This holds for every chapter of this file and the next.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans on God's first-person pronouns ("{{deity_pronoun:я|Я}}", "{{deity_pronoun:меня|Меня}}")
decisions.reason: God speaks in the first person through most of Isaiah. As in the Pentateuch and Psalms, every pronoun for God takes the deity_pronoun span, including a mid-sentence "я"; a pronoun that begins a sentence or a speech is written plainly with its capital, and reflexive свой and себя take none.

decisions.choice: Commands in the oracles: "〜せよ" (聞け, 耳を傾けよ) at Literal, "〜しなさい" at Balanced and Readable; prohibitions "〜するな" (L), "〜してはならない" (B), "〜してはいけない" (R), as Proverbs and Lamentations. God's words start without quotation marks, as the English (m3).
alternatives: "〜なさい" at Literal as in the Kings narratives
decisions.reason: The prophets are verse: the poetry books' command forms keep one system for every speaker in an oracle, and Literal's "〜せよ" keeps the bare Hebrew imperative. The English opens no quotation, so neither does the Japanese.

source.text: יָדַ֥ע שׁוֹר֙ קֹנֵ֔הוּ וַחֲמ֖וֹר אֵב֣וּס בְּעָלָ֑יו יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לֹ֣א יָדַ֔ע עַמִּ֖י לֹ֥א הִתְבּוֹנָֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: Knows an ox its owner, and a donkey [the] manger of its master; Israel not knows, my people not considers.

en.L: An ox knows its owner, \q and a donkey its master's manger; \q Israel does not know, \q {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people do not understand.
en.B: An ox recognizes its owner, \q a donkey the feeding trough of its master; \q but Israel does not know, \q {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people give it no thought.
en.R: An ox knows who owns it. \q A donkey knows where its master feeds it. \q But the people of Israel do not know {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \q My people do not stop to think.

es.L: El buey conoce a su dueño, \q y el asno el pesebre de su amo; \q Israel no conoce, \q {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo no entiende.
es.B: El buey reconoce a su dueño, \q y el asno el comedero de su amo; \q pero Israel no conoce, \q {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo no reflexiona.
es.R: El buey sabe quién es su dueño. \q El burro sabe dónde le da de comer su amo. \q Pero el pueblo de Israel no {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} conoce. \q Mi pueblo no se detiene a pensar.

fr.L: Le bœuf connaît son propriétaire, \q et l’âne la mangeoire de son maître ; \q Israël ne connaît pas, \q {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple ne comprend pas.
fr.B: Le bœuf reconnaît son propriétaire, \q et l’âne la mangeoire de son maître ; \q mais Israël ne connaît pas, \q {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple n’y prête aucune attention.
fr.R: Le bœuf sait à qui il appartient. \q L’âne sait où son maître lui donne à manger. \q Mais le peuple d’Israël ne {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} connaît pas. \q Mon peuple ne prend pas le temps de réfléchir.

sw.L: Ng'ombe humjua mwenyewe, \q na punda hori la bwana wake; \q Israeli hajui, \q watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} hawafahamu.
sw.B: Ng'ombe humtambua mwenye kumiliki, \q punda hulijua hori la bwana wake; \q lakini Israeli hajui, \q watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} hawalitafakari.
sw.R: Ng'ombe anamjua mwenye kumiliki. \q Punda anajua mahali bwana wake anapomlisha. \q Lakini watu wa Israeli hawanijui {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}. \q Watu wangu hawasimami kufikiri.

vi.L: Bò biết chủ mình, \q và lừa [biết] máng ăn của chủ nó; \q Y-sơ-ra-ên không biết, \q dân {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không suy hiểu.
vi.B: Con bò nhận biết chủ mình, \q con lừa biết máng cỏ của chủ nó; \q nhưng Y-sơ-ra-ên không biết, \q dân {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} chẳng hề suy nghĩ.
vi.R: Con bò biết ai là chủ nó. \q Con lừa biết chủ cho nó ăn ở đâu. \q Nhưng dân Y-sơ-ra-ên không biết {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. \q Dân {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} chẳng chịu suy nghĩ.

ko.L: 소는 자기 주인을 알고, \q 나귀는 자기 주인의 구유를 [안다]. \q 이스라엘은 알지 못하고, \q 내 백성은 깨닫지 못한다.
ko.B: 소도 제 주인을 알아보고, \q 나귀도 주인이 먹이를 주는 구유를 안다. \q 그러나 이스라엘은 알지 못하고, \q 내 백성은 생각조차 하지 않는다.
ko.R: 소는 자기 주인이 누구인지 안다. \q 나귀는 주인이 먹이를 어디서 주는지 안다. \q 그러나 이스라엘 백성은 나를 알지 못한다. \q 내 백성은 멈춰서 생각하지 않는다.

pt.L: O boi conhece o seu dono, \q e o jumento, a manjedoura do seu senhor; \q Israel não conhece, \q o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} povo não entende.
pt.B: O boi reconhece o seu dono, \q e o jumento, o cocho do seu senhor; \q mas Israel não conhece, \q o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} povo não pensa nisso.
pt.R: O boi sabe quem é o seu dono. \q O jumento sabe onde o seu dono lhe dá comida. \q Mas o povo de Israel não {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} conhece. \q O {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} povo não para para pensar.

am.L: በሬ ባለቤቱን ያውቃል፤ \q አህያም የጌታውን ግርግም፤ \q እስራኤል አያውቅም፤ \q ሕዝቤ አያስተውልም።
am.B: በሬ ባለቤቱን ያውቃል፤ \q አህያም የጌታውን ገንዳ ያውቃል፤ \q እስራኤል ግን አያውቅም፤ \q ሕዝቤ ልብ አይልም።
am.R: በሬ ባለቤቱ ማን እንደ ሆነ ያውቃል። \q አህያም ጌታው የት እንደሚመግበው ያውቃል። \q የእስራኤል ሕዝብ ግን እኔን አያውቁም። \q ሕዝቤ ቆም ብሎ አያስብም።

hi.L: बैल अपने मालिक को जानता है, \q और गधा अपने स्वामी की चरनी को; \q इस्राएल नहीं जानता, \q मेरी प्रजा नहीं समझती।
hi.B: बैल अपने मालिक को पहचानता है, \q और गधा अपने स्वामी की नाँद को; \q पर इस्राएल नहीं जानता, \q मेरी प्रजा इस पर ध्यान नहीं देती।
hi.R: बैल जानता है कि उसका मालिक कौन है। \q गधा जानता है कि उसका मालिक उसे कहाँ चारा देता है। \q पर इस्राएल के लोग मुझे नहीं जानते। \q मेरे लोग रुककर सोचते भी नहीं।

ru.L: Знает вол своего хозяина, \q и осёл — ясли своего господина; \q Израиль не знает, \q {{deity_pronoun:мой|Мой}} народ не разумеет.
ru.B: Вол узнаёт своего хозяина, \q осёл — кормушку своего господина; \q а Израиль не знает, \q {{deity_pronoun:мой|Мой}} народ не задумывается.
ru.R: Вол знает, кто его хозяин. \q Осёл знает, где его кормит хозяин. \q А народ Израиля не знает {{deity_pronoun:меня|Меня}}. \q Мой народ не хочет задуматься.

ja.L: 牛はその飼い主を知り、 \q ろばはその主人の飼い葉おけを[知っている]。 \q イスラエルは知らない。 \q わたしの民は悟らない。
ja.B: 牛は自分の持ち主を知っている。 \q ろばも主人の飼い葉おけを知っている。 \q しかしイスラエルは知らない。 \q わたしの民は、思いを向けようともしない。
ja.R: 牛は、だれが自分の持ち主かを知っている。 \q ろばは、主人がどこでえさをくれるかを知っている。 \q しかし、イスラエルの人々はわたしを知らない。 \q わたしの民は、立ち止まって考えようともしない。

decisions.choice: ox and donkey: work animals that know who feeds them
decisions.reason: The ox and the donkey were the common farm animals of Israel. Even they find their way back to their owner's feeding trough; God's people do not know the one who cares for them.

decisions.choice: Israel does not know: no object is stated; the one they do not know is God, their owner
decisions.reason: "Know" has no object, which makes the charge broader: Israel does not know at all. Set beside the ox and its owner, it means Israel does not know or acknowledge the God it belongs to (Hosea 4:1, 6; Jeremiah 8:7).

decisions.choice: understand: consider, pay attention
decisions.reason: The verb means to give careful thought to something. God's people do not stop to think about who he is or what he has done.

decisions.choice: the people of Israel do not know me
decisions.reason: Readable says "the people of Israel" for the name Israel and supplies "me", the one Israel does not know (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: "hawanijui mimi" (they do not know me)
decisions.reason: Readable names the one Israel does not know, God, as the English Readable does (m2).

decisions.choice: मेरी प्रजा
decisions.reason: God's "my people" is मेरी प्रजा at L and B, the word Matthew 13:15 and Acts 28:27 use for "this people" in Isaiah 6:10; Readable says मेरे लोग.

source.text: ה֣וֹי׀גּ֣וֹי חֹטֵ֗א עַ֚ם כֶּ֣בֶד עָוֺ֔ן זֶ֣רַע מְרֵעִ֔ים בָּנִ֖ים מַשְׁחִיתִ֑ים עָזְב֣וּ אֶת־יְהוָ֗ה נִֽאֲצ֛וּ אֶת־קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל נָזֹ֥רוּ אָחֽוֹר׃

records.literal_gloss: Woe, nation sinning, people heavy of iniquity, offspring of evildoers, children acting corruptly! They have forsaken Yahweh, they have spurned [the] Holy One of Israel, they have become estranged backward.

en.L: Woe, sinning nation, people heavy with iniquity, \q offspring of evildoers, children who act corruptly! \q They have forsaken {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, they have despised the Holy One of Israel, they have turned away backward.
en.B: Woe to a nation that sins, a people loaded down with guilt, \q the offspring of wrongdoers, children bent on corruption! \q They have left {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, they have scorned the Holy One of Israel, they have turned away from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and gone backward.
en.R: How terrible it will be for this sinful nation! Their guilt is a heavy load. \q They are a family of evil people, children who do corrupt things. \q They have left {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They have treated the Holy One of Israel with scorn. They have turned their backs on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: ¡Ay de la nación pecadora, del pueblo cargado de iniquidad, \q de la descendencia de malhechores, de los hijos que obran con corrupción! \q Han abandonado {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, han despreciado al Santo de Israel, se han alejado hacia atrás.
es.B: ¡Ay de una nación que peca, de un pueblo agobiado por la culpa, \q descendencia de malhechores, hijos entregados a la corrupción! \q Han dejado {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, han despreciado al Santo de Israel, se han apartado de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y han vuelto atrás.
es.R: ¡Qué terrible será para esta nación pecadora! Su culpa es una carga pesada. \q Son una familia de gente malvada, hijos que hacen cosas corruptas. \q Han dejado {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}. Han tratado con desprecio al Santo de Israel. Se han alejado de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.

fr.L: Malheur, nation pécheresse, peuple chargé d’iniquité, \q race de malfaiteurs, fils qui agissent de façon corrompue ! \q Ils ont abandonné {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, ils ont méprisé le Saint d’Israël, ils se sont détournés en arrière.
fr.B: Malheur à la nation qui pèche, au peuple accablé de fautes, \q à la race des méchants, aux enfants pervertis ! \q Ils ont quitté {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, ils ont méprisé le Saint d’Israël, ils se sont détournés de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} et sont partis en arrière.
fr.R: Quel malheur pour cette nation pécheresse ! Ses fautes sont un lourd fardeau. \q Ce sont des gens mauvais, des enfants qui font des choses corrompues. \q Ils ont quitté {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Ils ont traité le Saint d’Israël avec mépris. Ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ont tourné le dos.

sw.L: Ole, taifa lenye dhambi, watu waliolemewa na uovu, \q uzao wa watenda mabaya, wana wanaotenda kwa upotovu! \q Wamemwacha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, wamemdharau Mtakatifu wa Israeli, wamejitenga kwenda nyuma.
sw.B: Ole wao taifa lenye dhambi, watu waliolemewa na hatia, \q uzao wa watenda maovu, watoto waliozama katika upotovu! \q Wamemwacha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, wamemdharau Mtakatifu wa Israeli, wamemgeuka na kurudi nyuma.
sw.R: Itakuwa vibaya sana kwa taifa hili lenye dhambi! Hatia yao ni mzigo mzito. \q Wao ni jamaa ya watu waovu, watoto wanaofanya mambo machafu. \q Wamemwacha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Wamemdharau Mtakatifu wa Israeli. Wamempa kisogo.

vi.L: Khốn cho dân tộc phạm tội, dân nặng gánh gian ác, \q dòng dõi kẻ làm ác, con cái hành động bại hoại! \q Chúng đã lìa bỏ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, đã khinh dể Đấng Thánh của Y-sơ-ra-ên, đã xa lạ quay lưng đi.
vi.B: Khốn cho một dân tộc phạm tội, một dân chất đầy tội lỗi, \q dòng dõi của kẻ làm điều ác, con cái chuyên làm điều bại hoại! \q Chúng đã lìa bỏ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, đã khinh bỉ Đấng Thánh của Y-sơ-ra-ên, đã quay lưng lìa xa {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Thật khốn khổ cho dân tộc tội lỗi này! Tội lỗi của họ như một gánh nặng. \q Họ là dòng dõi của những kẻ gian ác, là con cái làm điều bại hoại. \q Họ đã lìa bỏ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Họ đã khinh bỉ Đấng Thánh của Y-sơ-ra-ên. Họ đã quay lưng với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 화가 있다, 죄를 짓는 민족, 죄악이 무거운 백성에게! \q 악을 행하는 자들의 자손, 타락한 자식들에게! \q 그들이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 버렸고, 이스라엘의 거룩하신 분을 업신여겼고, 뒤로 물러가 낯선 자가 되었다.
ko.B: 죄를 짓는 민족, 죄악을 무겁게 진 백성에게 화가 있다. \q 악한 자들의 자손, 타락한 자식들에게 화가 있다. \q 그들이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 버리고 이스라엘의 거룩하신 분을 멸시하며, 그분에게서 돌아서서 뒤로 가 버렸다.
ko.R: 죄를 짓는 이 민족에게 끔찍한 일이 닥칠 것이다! 그들의 죄는 무거운 짐과 같다. \q 그들은 악한 사람들의 자손이며, 타락한 일을 하는 자식들이다. \q 그들은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 버렸다. 이스라엘의 거룩하신 분을 업신여겼다. 그분에게 등을 돌렸다.

pt.L: Ai, nação pecadora, povo carregado de iniquidade, \q descendência de malfeitores, filhos que agem com corrupção! \q Abandonaram {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, desprezaram o Santo de Israel, afastaram-se para trás.
pt.B: Ai da nação que peca, do povo carregado de culpa, \q da descendência de malfeitores, dos filhos entregues à corrupção! \q Abandonaram {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, trataram com desprezo o Santo de Israel, viraram as costas para {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} e foram embora.
pt.R: Que desgraça vai cair sobre esta nação pecadora! A culpa dela é uma carga pesada. \q São uma família de gente má, filhos que fazem coisas corruptas. \q Abandonaram {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}. Trataram o Santo de Israel com desprezo. Viraram as costas para {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}.

am.L: ወዮ፣ ኃጢአተኛ ሕዝብ፣ በበደል የከበደ ወገን፣ \q የክፉ አድራጊዎች ዘር፣ የሚያበላሹ ልጆች! \q {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔርን|ያህዌን}} ትተዋል፤ የእስራኤልን ቅዱስ ንቀዋል፤ ወደ ኋላ ተመልሰው ራቁ።
am.B: ወዮ ኃጢአት ለሚሠራ ሕዝብ፣ በበደል ለተጫነ ወገን፣ \q ለክፉ አድራጊዎች ዘር፣ ለጥፋት ላዘነበሉ ልጆች! \q {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔርን|ያህዌን}} ተዉ፤ የእስራኤልን ቅዱስ አቃለሉ፤ ከእርሱ ርቀው ወደ ኋላ ሄዱ።
am.R: ለዚህ ኃጢአተኛ ሕዝብ ወዮለት! በደሉ እንደ ከባድ ሸክም ነው። \q የክፉ ሰዎች ቤተሰብ ናቸው፤ ብልሹ ነገር የሚያደርጉ ልጆች ናቸው። \q {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔርን|ያህዌን}} ትተዋል። የእስራኤልን ቅዱስ በንቀት አይተዋል። ጀርባቸውን ሰጥተውታል።

hi.L: हाय, पापी जाति, अधर्म से लदी हुई प्रजा, \q कुकर्मियों का वंश, बिगाड़ करनेवाले बच्चे! \q उन्होंने {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} को त्याग दिया है, उन्होंने इस्राएल के पवित्र को तुच्छ जाना है, वे पीछे की ओर फिरकर पराए हो गए हैं।
hi.B: हाय उस देश पर जो पाप करता है, उस प्रजा पर जो दोष के बोझ से दबी है, \q कुकर्मियों की सन्तान पर, बिगाड़ पर तुले बच्चों पर! \q उन्होंने {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} को छोड़ दिया है, उन्होंने इस्राएल के पवित्र का तिरस्कार किया है, वे उनसे मुँह मोड़कर पीछे हट गए हैं।
hi.R: इस पापी देश के लिए कितना भयानक होगा! उनका दोष एक भारी बोझ है। \q वे दुष्ट लोगों का परिवार हैं, ऐसे बच्चे जो बुरे काम करते हैं। \q उन्होंने {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} को छोड़ दिया है। उन्होंने इस्राएल के पवित्र का अपमान किया है। उन्होंने उनकी ओर से पीठ फेर ली है।

ru.L: Горе, народ грешный, люди, отягощённые беззаконием, \q семя злодеев, дети, поступающие порочно! \q Они оставили {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Яхве}}, презрели Святого Израиля, отвернулись назад.
ru.B: Горе народу, который грешит, людям, нагруженным виной, \q потомству злодеев, детям, склонным к порче! \q Они оставили {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Яхве}}, отнеслись с презрением к Святому Израиля, отвернулись от {{deity_pronoun:него|Него}} и пошли назад.
ru.R: Беда ждёт этот грешный народ! Их вина — тяжёлый груз. \q Это семья злых людей, дети, которые делают порочное. \q Они оставили {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Яхве}}. Они отнеслись к Святому Израиля с презрением. Они повернулись к {{deity_pronoun:нему|Нему}} спиной.

ja.L: ああ、災いだ、罪を犯す国、咎の重い民、 \q 悪を行う者たちの子孫、堕落した子らは！ \q 彼らは{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}を捨て、イスラエルの聖なる方を侮り、背を向けて離れ去った。
ja.B: ああ、災いだ、罪を犯す国、咎を負って重くなった民、 \q 悪を行う者たちの子孫、堕落しきった子らは！ \q 彼らは{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}を捨て、イスラエルの聖なる方をさげすみ、その方に背を向けて去って行った。
ja.R: ああ、この罪深い国は、なんとひどい目にあうことか！その罪は重い荷物のようだ。 \q 彼らは悪い者たちの一族、悪いことばかりする子どもたちだ。 \q 彼らは{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}を捨てた。イスラエルの聖なる方をばかにした。その方に背を向けたのだ。

decisions.choice: the Holy One of Israel: the God who is wholly other and pure, and who has bound himself to Israel
decisions.reason: This is Isaiah's own title for God. It appears about twenty-five times in the book, through every part of it, and only a few times elsewhere (2 Kings 19:22, which is Isaiah's word to Hezekiah; Psalms 71:22; 78:41; 89:19; Jeremiah 50:29; 51:5). "Holy" means set apart: God is unlike everything he has made and pure of every wrong, and Isaiah heard the seraphim call him "holy, holy, holy" (6:3). "Of Israel" says that this holy God has made himself Israel's own. That makes their contempt for him the more shocking here, and his promise to redeem them the more sure (41:14; 43:14).

decisions.choice: woe: a cry of grief over those facing judgment
decisions.reason: The word was cried out in mourning for the dead (1 Kings 13:30; Jeremiah 22:18). The prophets use it to announce disaster on those who deserve it, as if their funeral had already begun (5:8-22; Amos 5:18).

decisions.choice: estranged backward: they have turned their backs and gone away
decisions.reason: The verb means to become a stranger. With "backward" it pictures people who have turned away from God and walk off in the opposite direction (Jeremiah 7:24).

decisions.choice: turned away from him and gone backward / turned their backs on him
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the one they have turned from, God, which the Hebrew leaves implied.

decisions.choice: ¡Ay de ...! (L, B); ¡Qué terrible será para ...! (R)
decisions.reason: The cry hoy is rendered as the terms note sets it for Isaiah and Jeremiah, as Matthew 23:13 does: L and B join the cry to those it is aimed at with "¡Ay de ...!", and R says what the cry means, as the English R does. Book-wide choice, recorded once for chapters 1-20.

decisions.choice: el Santo de Israel
decisions.reason: Isaiah's title for God is "el Santo de Israel" at every level, as 2 Kings 19:22 and Psalm 71:22 already have it in Spanish.

decisions.choice: *hoy*: "Ole" (L), "Ole wao" (B), "Itakuwa vibaya sana kwa" (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *hoy* in Isaiah and Jeremiah, as Luke 6:24 (terms note). Recorded once for this block.

decisions.choice: "Mtakatifu wa Israeli"
decisions.reason: God's title in Isaiah, as 2 Kings 19:22 and Psalm 71:22, at every level (m1).

decisions.choice: "Malheur, ..." (L); "Malheur à ..." (B); "Quel malheur pour ... !" (R)
decisions.reason: The cry *hoy* is "Malheur" at Literal and Balanced and "Quel malheur pour" at Readable, as Matthew 23:13, for the whole book.

decisions.choice: "le Saint d’Israël"
decisions.reason: Isaiah’s title for God is "le Saint d’Israël" at every level, as 2 Kings 19:22 and Psalm 78:41, for the whole book.

decisions.choice: "Khốn cho" (L, B); "Thật khốn khổ cho" (R)
decisions.reason: The terms note's form for "hoy" as a threat, used through the book, as Matthew 11:21; "Than ôi" is kept for a funeral cry.

decisions.choice: "Đấng Thánh của Y-sơ-ra-ên"
decisions.reason: The title as published in 2 Kings 19:22 and Psalm 78:41, used unchanged through Isaiah.

decisions.choice: "~에게 화가 있다" (L, B); "~에게 끔찍한 일이 닥칠 것이다" (R) for *hoy*
decisions.reason: The terms note's forms (Matthew 23:13 L, R). Literal puts "화가 있다" first to keep the cry at the head of the line; "화 있을진저" is archaic.

decisions.choice: "이스라엘의 거룩하신 분"
decisions.reason: The prophet speaks of God, so the title takes the honorific; when God names himself it is "이스라엘의 거룩한 이" (terms note).

decisions.choice: Ai ... / Ai de ... (L, B); Que desgraça vai cair sobre ... (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: the cry hoy (m2) is "Ai" at Literal and "Ai de"/"Ai da" at Balanced, the Portuguese cry of grief and warning every reader knows from the prophets and the Gospels ("Ai de vocês", docs/portuguese-style.md section 6). Readable says what the cry announces, "Que desgraça vai cair sobre", where the English Readable says "How terrible it will be for". The series of woes in 5:8-22 and 10:1, 10:5 follows this.

decisions.choice: o Santo de Israel (every level)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: Isaiah's own title for God (m1), about twenty-five times, is "o Santo de Israel" at every level, with capitals, as 2 Kings 19:22 and Psalm 71:22 have it in Portuguese and as the English keeps it at Readable. The wording does not change between chapters.

decisions.choice: woe (hoy) "ወዮ" at every level (Readable "ወዮለት"); the Holy One of Israel "የእስራኤል ቅዱስ", as 2 Kings 19:22
decisions.reason: Both recur through the book. "ወዮ" is the Amharic cry of grief and warning over those facing judgment, so it stands where the English Balanced and Readable say "Woe to" and "How terrible it will be"; the title of God keeps the wording of 2 Kings 19:22, which Isaiah 37:23 repeats.

decisions.choice: nation (goy) "ሕዝብ" and people (ʿam) "ወገን" where the two stand side by side
decisions.reason: The Hebrew pairs two words for a people; Amharic keeps the pair with "ሕዝብ" and "ወገን", as the Psalms do. Where ʿam stands alone it is "ሕዝብ" ("ሕዝቤ", my people).

decisions.choice: हाय (L, B); X के लिए कितना भयानक होगा! (R)
decisions.reason: The cry hoy is हाय at L and B, as the terms note sets it for the Prophets and as Matthew 23:13 has "तुम पर हाय"; Readable says what the cry means, as the English Readable does. Book-wide choice.

decisions.choice: इस्राएल का पवित्र
decisions.reason: Isaiah's title for God is इस्राएल का पवित्र at every level, the form the terms note fixes for the whole book (oblique इस्राएल के पवित्र). No noun is added after पवित्र: the adjective used as a noun is Hindi's way of saying "the Holy One", and adding परमेश्वर would turn the title into a description.

decisions.choice: जाति (L); देश (B, R)
decisions.reason: goy is जाति at Literal and देश at Balanced and Readable, where जाति would also suggest caste, as the poetry note sets for "the nations".

decisions.choice: "Святой Израиля" for the Holy One of Israel, the same at every level
decisions.reason: Isaiah's own title for God, used through the whole book; one form at every level, as in Psalms 71:22 and 78:41 in this translation and as the Prophets note settles. The genitive "Израиля" is modern Russian; the older possessive "Израилев" is avoided.

decisions.choice: "Горе" (L, B); "Беда ждёт..." (R)
decisions.reason: The prophets' cry of mourning over those facing judgment is "Горе" at Literal and Balanced, as in the New Testament's "Горе вам". Readable, like the English, says what the cry means, with one wording through the book.

decisions.choice: hoy "woe": "ああ、災いだ、Xは！" (L, B), with the Hebrew's nouns kept in order before the inverted "は"; Readable "ああ、Xはなんとひどい目にあうことか！" as the English Readable "How terrible it will be for". The cry 'oy ("woe is me / us", 3:9, 6:5) is "ああ、わたしは災いだ" (L, B), as Lamentations.
decisions.reason: The style guide gives "災いだ" for woe; the inverted order lets the Hebrew's string of addresses come first, as in Isaiah 5:8-22 where hoy opens six sayings. Readable explains the grief and the coming judgment (m2) in everyday words.

decisions.choice: qedosh Yisra'el "the Holy One of Israel": "イスラエルの聖なる方" at every level, as 2 Kings 19:22.
decisions.reason: Isaiah's title for God (about 25 times) needs one fixed form; "方" keeps it personal and respectful, and the reader of 2 Kings 19 has already met it. The English Readable keeps the title too.

source.text: עַ֣ל מֶ֥ה תֻכּ֛וּ ע֖וֹד תּוֹסִ֣יפוּ סָרָ֑ה כָּל־רֹ֣אשׁ לָחֳלִ֔י וְכָל־לֵבָ֖ב דַּוָּֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: On what will you be struck again? You will add rebellion. All [the] head [is] for sickness, and all [the] heart faint.

en.L: On what [part] will you be struck again, [as] you keep adding rebellion? \q The whole head [is] sick, and the whole heart faint.
en.B: Where else can you be struck, as you go on rebelling? \q The head is sick all over; the heart is weak through and through.
en.R: Where else can you be beaten, since you keep turning against God? \q You are like a body whose head is sick all over and whose heart is weak.

es.L: ¿Sobre qué [parte] {{plural_you:serán golpeados|seréis golpeados}} aún, [si] {{plural_you:siguen añadiendo|seguís añadiendo}} rebelión? \q Toda la cabeza [está] enferma, y todo el corazón desfallecido.
es.B: ¿Dónde más {{plural_you:los pueden golpear|os pueden golpear}}, si {{plural_you:siguen rebelándose|seguís rebelándoos}}? \q La cabeza está enferma por completo; el corazón, débil del todo.
es.R: ¿Dónde más {{plural_you:los pueden castigar|os pueden castigar}}, si {{plural_you:siguen poniéndose|seguís poniéndoos}} en contra de Dios? \q {{plural_you:Son|Sois}} como un cuerpo con la cabeza toda enferma y el corazón débil.

fr.L: Sur quoi serez-vous encore frappés, [vous qui] continuez à vous révolter ? \q Toute la tête [est] malade, et tout le cœur languissant.
fr.B: Où pourriez-vous encore être frappés, vous qui persistez dans la révolte ? \q La tête est malade tout entière, le cœur est faible tout entier.
fr.R: Où peut-on encore vous frapper, puisque vous continuez à vous tourner contre Dieu ? \q Vous êtes comme un corps dont la tête est malade de partout et dont le cœur n’a plus de force.

sw.L: Mtapigwa wapi tena, [mkiwa] mnaendelea kuongeza uasi? \q Kichwa kizima [ni] kigonjwa, na moyo wote umezimia.
sw.B: Mtapigwa wapi tena, maana mnaendelea kuasi? \q Kichwa kizima ni kigonjwa, moyo wote umedhoofika.
sw.R: Mtapigwa wapi tena, kwa kuwa mnaendelea kumwasi Mungu? \q Mko kama mwili ambao kichwa chake ni kigonjwa kabisa na moyo wake ni dhaifu.

vi.L: Các người còn bị đánh vào [chỗ] nào nữa, [khi] các người cứ thêm sự phản loạn? \q Cả cái đầu [đều] bệnh, cả tấm lòng mòn mỏi.
vi.B: Các người còn có thể bị đánh vào đâu nữa, khi các người cứ tiếp tục phản loạn? \q Cả đầu đều đau ốm, cả lòng đều yếu mòn.
vi.R: Các người còn muốn bị đánh vào chỗ nào nữa, khi các người cứ mãi chống lại Đức Chúa Trời? \q Các người giống như một thân thể đầu đau khắp cả, lòng yếu đuối rã rời.

ko.L: 너희가 어디를 더 맞으려고 [하느냐], 계속 반역을 더하면서? \q 머리는 온통 병들었고, 마음은 온통 지쳐 있다.
ko.B: 너희가 계속 반역하니, 어디를 더 맞겠느냐? \q 머리는 성한 데 없이 병들었고, 심장은 속속들이 약해졌다.
ko.R: 너희가 계속 하나님을 거역하니, 몸의 어디를 더 맞을 셈이냐? \q 너희는 머리가 온통 병들고 심장이 약해진 몸과 같다.

pt.L: Em que [parte] vocês ainda serão feridos, [se] continuam a acrescentar rebeldia? \q Toda a cabeça [está] doente, e todo o coração, desfalecido.
pt.B: Onde mais vocês podem ser feridos, já que continuam a se rebelar? \q A cabeça está doente por inteiro; o coração está completamente fraco.
pt.R: Onde mais vocês podem apanhar, se continuam se voltando contra Deus? \q Vocês são como um corpo com a cabeça toda doente e o coração fraco.

am.L: ዓመፅን እየጨመራችሁ በምን [ስፍራ] እንደ ገና ትመታላችሁ? \q ራስ ሁሉ ለሕመም፣ ልብም ሁሉ ደካማ [ነው]።
am.B: ማመፃችሁን ስትቀጥሉ፣ ከዚህ በላይ የት ልትመቱ ትችላላችሁ? \q ራሱ ሁሉ ታሟል፤ ልቡም ፈጽሞ ደክሟል።
am.R: በእግዚአብሔር ላይ ማመፃችሁን ስለ ቀጠላችሁ፣ ከዚህ በላይ የት ልትደበደቡ ትችላላችሁ? \q ራሱ ሁሉ እንደ ታመመና ልቡ እንደ ደከመ አካል ሆናችኋል።

hi.L: तुम किस [अंग] पर फिर मारे जाओगे, [जब] तुम विद्रोह बढ़ाते ही जाते हो? \q सारा सिर रोगी [है], और सारा हृदय निर्बल।
hi.B: तुम्हें और कहाँ मारा जा सकता है, जब तुम विद्रोह करते ही जाते हो? \q सिर पूरा का पूरा रोगी है; हृदय भीतर तक निर्बल है।
hi.R: तुम्हें और कहाँ पीटा जाए, जब तुम परमेश्वर के विरुद्ध होते ही जाते हो? \q तुम उस शरीर के समान हो जिसका पूरा सिर रोगी है और जिसका हृदय कमज़ोर है।

ru.L: Куда [ещё] бить вас, [раз] вы продолжаете восстание? \q Вся голова [в] болезни, и всё сердце изнемогло.
ru.B: Куда ещё вас бить, если вы всё восстаёте? \q Голова больна вся, сердце изнемогло совсем.
ru.R: Куда ещё вас бить, если вы всё время восстаёте против Бога? \q Вы как тело, у которого вся голова больна и сердце ослабело.

ja.L: あなたがたは、なおどこを打たれようというのか、背きを重ねながら？ \q 頭は全体が病み、心は全体が弱り果てている。
ja.B: あなたがたは背き続けているが、これ以上どこを打たれようというのか？ \q 頭はどこも病み、心はすっかり弱っている。
ja.R: あなたたちは、神に逆らい続けている。これ以上、体のどこを打たれたいのか？ \q あなたたちは、頭がどこも病気で、心臓が弱っている体のようだ。

decisions.choice: on what: where on the body can you still be struck
alternatives: Why will you still be struck?
decisions.reason: The two words can mean "why" or "on what". Verse 6 describes a body with no sound spot left, which favors "on what [place]": the nation has been beaten everywhere already. Read as "why", the question asks why they invite more blows by rebelling.

decisions.choice: rebellion: turning aside, revolt
decisions.reason: The noun means turning away from the right path, used of revolt against God (Deuteronomy 13:6; Jeremiah 28:16).

decisions.choice: the whole head ... the whole heart: the nation pictured as a beaten body
decisions.reason: The head and the heart stand for the whole person, from top to center. Judah is pictured as a body covered in wounds, the blows being the disasters already suffered (verse 7).

decisions.choice: turning against God ... You are like a body
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one they rebel against and explains that the head and heart are a picture of the nation.

decisions.choice: plural_you span: ustedes forms by default, vosotros forms as the alternative
decisions.reason: Every plural "you" in the oracles to Judah, whether pronoun, verb or possessive, is a plural_you span: Latin American ustedes by default, the vosotros forms of Spain as the alternative, with the verb inside the span. Where su could be misread, the span takes in the noun (su tierra / vuestra tierra). Book-wide choice, recorded once for chapters 1-20.

decisions.choice: the prophet says "các người" to the people
decisions.reason: The terms note: the prophet rebuking the people says "các người"; God speaking to them as a group says "các ngươi" (verses 11-20). Verses 5-10 are the prophet's voice ("us" in verse 9, "our God" in verse 10).

decisions.choice: God and the prophet address Israel, Judah and Jerusalem's people in the plural as "あなたがた" (L, B) and "あなたたち" (R); a city or people addressed in the singular (Zion, Jerusalem, Jacob) is "あなた". "おまえ / おまえたち" is kept for taunts against hostile kings and nations (Assyria, Babylon) and for a scornful word to a single official, as in 2 Kings 19.
decisions.reason: Even in rebuke God speaks to his own people as a father to children he has raised (1:2); "おまえたち" would turn the lawsuit into contempt and would leave nothing harsher for the taunts over the nations. This follows the style guide's divine address and Lamentations, where Zion is "あなた".

source.text: מִכַּף־רֶ֤גֶל וְעַד־רֹאשׁ֙ אֵֽין־בּ֣וֹ מְתֹ֔ם פֶּ֥צַע וְחַבּוּרָ֖ה וּמַכָּ֣ה טְרִיָּ֑ה לֹא־זֹ֨רוּ֙ וְלֹ֣א חֻבָּ֔שׁוּ וְלֹ֥א רֻכְּכָ֖ה בַּשָּֽׁמֶן׃

records.literal_gloss: From [the] sole of [the] foot and to [the] head there is not in it soundness: bruise and welt and wound fresh; not they have been pressed out and not bound up and not softened with oil.

en.L: From the sole of the foot even to the head there is no soundness in it: \q bruises and welts and fresh wounds; \q they have not been pressed out, and not bound up, \q and not softened with oil.
en.B: There is no healthy spot from the bottom of the foot up to the head: \q bruises, stripes, wounds still raw. \q No one has squeezed them clean, no one has bound them, \q no one has eased them with oil.
en.R: From your feet to your head, no part of your body is healthy. \q You are covered with bruises, cuts, and fresh wounds. \q No one has cleaned them or wrapped them in bandages. \q No one has put soothing oil on them.

es.L: Desde la planta del pie hasta la cabeza no hay en él nada sano: \q golpes, verdugones y heridas recientes; \q no han sido exprimidas ni vendadas, \q ni suavizadas con aceite.
es.B: No hay un lugar sano desde la planta del pie hasta la cabeza: \q moretones, marcas de azotes, heridas todavía abiertas. \q Nadie las ha limpiado, nadie las ha vendado, \q nadie las ha aliviado con aceite.
es.R: Desde los pies hasta la cabeza, ninguna parte de {{plural_you:su cuerpo|vuestro cuerpo}} está sana. \q {{plural_you:Están cubiertos|Estáis cubiertos}} de moretones, cortadas y heridas frescas. \q Nadie las ha limpiado ni las ha envuelto con vendas. \q Nadie les ha puesto aceite para calmar el dolor.

fr.L: De la plante du pied jusqu’à la tête, il n’y a rien d’intact en lui : \q contusions, meurtrissures et plaies vives ; \q elles n’ont pas été pressées, ni bandées, \q ni adoucies avec de l’huile.
fr.B: De la plante des pieds jusqu’à la tête, plus rien n’est sain : \q bleus, marques de coups, plaies encore à vif. \q Personne ne les a nettoyées, personne ne les a pansées, \q personne ne les a soulagées avec de l’huile.
fr.R: Des pieds à la tête, aucune partie de votre corps n’est en bonne santé. \q Vous êtes couverts de bleus, de coupures et de plaies toutes fraîches. \q Personne ne les a nettoyées ni entourées de bandages. \q Personne n’y a mis d’huile pour les calmer.

sw.L: Tangu wayo wa mguu hata kichwa hakuna uzima ndani yake: \q michubuko na makovu na majeraha mabichi; \q hayajakamuliwa, wala hayajafungwa, \q wala hayajalainishwa kwa mafuta.
sw.B: Hakuna sehemu iliyo nzima tangu chini ya mguu hadi kichwani: \q michubuko, alama za fimbo, majeraha yaliyo bado mabichi. \q Hakuna aliyeyakamua yawe safi, hakuna aliyeyafunga, \q hakuna aliyeyatuliza kwa mafuta.
sw.R: Tangu miguuni hadi kichwani, hakuna sehemu ya mwili wenu iliyo nzima. \q Mmejaa michubuko, mikwaruzo na majeraha mabichi. \q Hakuna aliyeyasafisha wala kuyafunga kwa vitambaa. \q Hakuna aliyeyapaka mafuta ya kutuliza.

vi.L: Từ lòng bàn chân cho đến đầu, chẳng có chỗ nào lành: \q [chỉ] vết bầm, lằn roi và vết thương còn mới; \q chưa được nặn mủ, chưa được băng bó, \q cũng chưa được xoa dầu cho dịu.
vi.B: Từ gan bàn chân lên tới đầu, không còn chỗ nào lành lặn: \q toàn là vết bầm, lằn roi, vết thương còn tươi. \q Chẳng ai nặn rửa, chẳng ai băng bó, \q chẳng ai xoa dầu cho dịu.
vi.R: Từ chân đến đầu, không một chỗ nào trên thân thể các người còn lành. \q Khắp mình đầy vết bầm, vết rách và vết thương còn mới. \q Không ai rửa sạch hay băng bó chúng. \q Không ai xoa dầu cho dịu đau.

ko.L: 발바닥에서 머리까지 그 안에 성한 곳이 없다. \q 멍과 채찍 자국과 생생한 상처뿐이다. \q 그것들은 짜내지도 싸매지도 않았고, \q 기름으로 부드럽게 하지도 않았다.
ko.B: 발바닥부터 머리끝까지 성한 데가 없다. \q 멍과 채찍 자국과 아직 아물지 않은 상처뿐이다. \q 아무도 고름을 짜내지 않았고 아무도 싸매 주지 않았으며, \q 아무도 기름을 발라 주지 않았다.
ko.R: 너희 몸은 발에서 머리까지 건강한 데가 하나도 없다. \q 온몸이 멍과 찢긴 자국과 새 상처투성이다. \q 아무도 그 상처를 씻어 주거나 붕대로 감아 주지 않았다. \q 아무도 아픔을 덜어 주는 기름을 발라 주지 않았다.

pt.L: Da planta do pé até a cabeça não há nele [parte] sã: \q contusões, vergões e feridas recentes; \q não foram espremidas, nem atadas, \q nem amolecidas com azeite.
pt.B: Não há um lugar sadio da sola do pé até a cabeça: \q hematomas, marcas de chicote, feridas ainda em carne viva. \q Ninguém as limpou, ninguém as enfaixou, \q ninguém as aliviou com azeite.
pt.R: Dos pés até a cabeça, nenhuma parte do corpo de vocês tem saúde. \q Vocês estão cobertos de manchas roxas, cortes e feridas abertas. \q Ninguém limpou as feridas nem pôs curativos nelas. \q Ninguém passou óleo nelas para aliviar a dor.

am.L: ከእግር ጫማ እስከ ራስ ድረስ በእርሱ ጤንነት የለም፤ \q ቁስልና ሰንበር፣ አዲስም ቁስል [ብቻ ነው]፤ \q አልተጨመቁም፤ አልተጠገኑም፤ \q በዘይትም አልለዘቡም።
am.B: ከእግር ጫማ አንሥቶ እስከ ራስ ድረስ ጤነኛ ቦታ የለም፤ \q ብልዝ፣ ሰንበርና ገና ያልደረቀ ቁስል ብቻ ነው። \q ማንም አላጸዳቸውም፤ ማንም አላሰራቸውም፤ \q ማንም በዘይት አላስታገሣቸውም።
am.R: ከእግራችሁ እስከ ራሳችሁ ድረስ ጤነኛ የሆነ የአካል ክፍል የላችሁም። \q በብልዝ፣ በሰንበርና በአዲስ ቁስል ተሸፍናችኋል። \q ማንም አላጠባቸውም፤ በጨርቅም አላሰራቸውም። \q ማንም የሚያስታግሥ ዘይት አልቀባቸውም።

hi.L: पाँव के तलवे से लेकर सिर तक उसमें कुछ भी स्वस्थ नहीं: \q चोट और घाव और ताज़े ज़ख़्म; \q वे न दबाकर साफ़ किए गए, और न बाँधे गए, \q और न तेल से नरम किए गए।
hi.B: पाँव के तलवे से सिर तक कोई अंग स्वस्थ नहीं: \q चोटें, कोड़ों के निशान, कच्चे घाव। \q किसी ने उन्हें दबाकर साफ़ नहीं किया, किसी ने उन पर पट्टी नहीं बाँधी, \q किसी ने तेल लगाकर उन्हें आराम नहीं दिया।
hi.R: तुम्हारे पाँव से सिर तक शरीर का कोई भाग स्वस्थ नहीं है। \q तुम चोटों, कटे घावों और ताज़े ज़ख़्मों से भरे हुए हो। \q किसी ने उन्हें साफ़ नहीं किया, न उन पर पट्टी बाँधी। \q किसी ने उन पर आराम देनेवाला तेल नहीं लगाया।

ru.L: От подошвы ноги и до головы нет в нём здорового места: \q ушибы, и рубцы, и свежие раны; \q не выдавлены [они], и не перевязаны, \q и не смягчены маслом.
ru.B: Нет здорового места от ступни до головы: \q синяки, полосы от ударов, незажившие раны. \q Никто их не очистил, никто не перевязал, \q никто не облегчил их маслом.
ru.R: С ног до головы у вас нет ни одного здорового места. \q Вы все в синяках, порезах и свежих ранах. \q Никто их не промыл и не перевязал. \q Никто не смазал их маслом, чтобы унять боль.

ja.L: 足の裏から頭まで、そこには健やかなところがない。 \q 打ち傷、みみずばれ、生々しい傷。 \q それらは絞り出されず、包まれず、 \q 油で和らげられてもいない。
ja.B: 足の裏から頭まで、健やかなところは一つもない。 \q 打ち傷、むちの跡、まだ生々しい傷。 \q だれもそれを絞って清めず、包帯もせず、 \q 油で和らげる者もいない。
ja.R: 足から頭まで、体に健康なところは一つもない。 \q あなたたちは、打ち傷や切り傷や新しい傷だらけだ。 \q だれも、それを洗いもせず、包帯もしていない。 \q 痛みを和らげる油を塗ってくれる者もいない。

decisions.choice: bruise, welt, wound: the marks of a severe beating
decisions.reason: The three words describe blows: bruises, the stripes left by a lash (Proverbs 20:30), and open wounds still fresh and raw.

decisions.choice: pressed out, bound up, softened with oil: the care given to wounds
decisions.reason: A wound was cleaned by pressing out the pus, then bandaged and soothed with olive oil (Luke 10:34; Jeremiah 8:22). None of this has been done: the nation lies wounded and untended.

decisions.choice: no one has ...
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verbs are passive ("they have not been pressed out"). Balanced and Readable say "no one has", which keeps the sense that the wounds are left untended. Readable also says "your body" for "it".

source.text: אַרְצְכֶ֣ם שְׁמָמָ֔ה עָרֵיכֶ֖ם שְׂרֻפ֣וֹת אֵ֑שׁ אַדְמַתְכֶ֗ם לְנֶגְדְּכֶם֙ זָרִים֙ אֹכְלִ֣ים אֹתָ֔הּ וּשְׁמָמָ֖ה כְּמַהְפֵּכַ֥ת זָרִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: Your land [is] a desolation, your cities burned [with] fire; your ground, before you strangers [are] devouring it, and desolation like [the] overthrow of strangers.

en.L: Your land [is] a desolation; \q your cities [are] burned with fire; \q your ground: before your eyes strangers are devouring it, \q and [it is] a desolation, like an overthrow by strangers.
en.B: Your country lies in ruins, \q your towns are burned down; \q foreigners eat up your fields while you watch, \q and it is ruined like a land that foreigners have torn down.
en.R: Your country has been ruined. Your towns have been burned. \q Foreigners are taking the crops from your fields while you watch. \q Everything is destroyed, as when an enemy army tears a land apart.

es.L: {{plural_you:Su tierra|Vuestra tierra}} [es] una desolación; \q {{plural_you:sus ciudades|vuestras ciudades}} [están] quemadas por el fuego; \q {{plural_you:su suelo|vuestro suelo}}: delante de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} los extranjeros lo devoran, \q y [es] una desolación, como una destrucción por extranjeros.
es.B: {{plural_you:Su país|Vuestro país}} está en ruinas, \q {{plural_you:sus pueblos|vuestros pueblos}} incendiados; \q los extranjeros se comen {{plural_you:sus campos|vuestros campos}} mientras {{plural_you:ustedes miran|vosotros miráis}}, \q y queda arrasado como una tierra que los extranjeros han destruido.
es.R: {{plural_you:Su país|Vuestro país}} ha sido arruinado. {{plural_you:Sus pueblos|Vuestros pueblos}} han sido quemados. \q Los extranjeros se llevan las cosechas de {{plural_you:sus campos|vuestros campos}} mientras {{plural_you:ustedes miran|vosotros miráis}}. \q Todo está destruido, como cuando un ejército enemigo destroza un país.

fr.L: Votre pays [est] une désolation, \q vos villes [sont] brûlées par le feu ; \q votre sol, sous vos yeux des étrangers le dévorent, \q et [c’est] une désolation, comme un bouleversement par des étrangers.
fr.B: Votre pays est en ruine, \q vos villes sont incendiées ; \q des étrangers dévorent vos champs sous vos yeux, \q et tout est dévasté comme un pays renversé par des étrangers.
fr.R: Votre pays a été détruit. Vos villes ont été brûlées. \q Des étrangers prennent les récoltes de vos champs sous vos yeux. \q Tout est dévasté, comme quand une armée ennemie ravage un pays.

sw.L: Nchi yenu [ni] ukiwa; \q miji yenu [imeteketezwa] kwa moto; \q ardhi yenu, mbele yenu wageni wanaila, \q nayo [ni] ukiwa, kama uliopinduliwa na wageni.
sw.B: Nchi yenu imekuwa magofu, \q miji yenu imeteketezwa kwa moto; \q wageni wanayala mashamba yenu mkiwa mnatazama, \q nayo imeharibiwa kama nchi iliyobomolewa na wageni.
sw.R: Nchi yenu imeharibiwa. Miji yenu imechomwa moto. \q Wageni wanachukua mazao ya mashamba yenu nanyi mnatazama tu. \q Kila kitu kimeharibiwa, kama jeshi la adui linapoiharibu nchi.

vi.L: Xứ các người [là] nơi hoang tàn; \q các thành các người [bị] lửa thiêu đốt; \q đất ruộng các người, ngay trước mắt các người kẻ lạ đang nuốt lấy, \q và [nó là] cảnh hoang tàn, như bị kẻ lạ lật đổ.
vi.B: Xứ các người bị tàn phá, \q các thành các người bị lửa thiêu rụi; \q ngay trước mắt các người, người ngoại bang ăn nuốt hoa màu ruộng đất các người, \q và xứ hoang tàn như một vùng bị người ngoại bang lật đổ.
vi.R: Đất nước các người đã bị tàn phá. Các thành các người đã bị đốt cháy. \q Người nước ngoài đang lấy hết hoa màu trên đồng ruộng ngay trước mắt các người. \q Mọi thứ đều bị hủy phá, như khi một đạo quân thù xé nát một xứ.

ko.L: 너희 땅은 황폐하고, \q 너희 성읍들은 불에 탔다. \q 너희 토지는 너희 눈앞에서 낯선 자들이 그것을 먹어 치우고, \q 낯선 자들이 뒤엎은 것처럼 황폐하다.
ko.B: 너희 나라는 폐허가 되었고, \q 너희 성읍들은 불에 타 버렸다. \q 너희가 보는 앞에서 이방 사람들이 너희 밭의 소출을 먹어 치우니, \q 이방 사람들이 휩쓸고 간 땅처럼 황폐하다.
ko.R: 너희 나라는 망가졌다. 너희 성읍들은 불타 버렸다. \q 너희가 보는 앞에서 외국 사람들이 너희 밭의 곡식을 빼앗아 간다. \q 적군이 휩쓸고 간 땅처럼 모든 것이 부서졌다.

pt.L: A terra de vocês [é] uma desolação; \q as suas cidades [estão] queimadas a fogo; \q o seu solo: diante dos seus olhos estrangeiros o devoram, \q e [é] uma desolação, como uma destruição por estrangeiros.
pt.B: O país de vocês está em ruínas, \q as suas cidades foram queimadas; \q estrangeiros devoram os seus campos diante dos seus olhos, \q e tudo está arrasado como uma terra que estrangeiros derrubaram.
pt.R: O país de vocês foi arruinado. As suas cidades foram queimadas. \q Os estrangeiros estão levando as colheitas dos seus campos, e vocês só ficam olhando. \q Tudo está destruído, como quando um exército inimigo arrasa uma terra.

am.L: ምድራችሁ ባድማ [ናት]፤ \q ከተሞቻችሁ በእሳት የተቃጠሉ [ናቸው]፤ \q መሬታችሁን በፊታችሁ ባዕዳን ይበሉታል፤ \q በባዕዳን እንደ ተገለበጠችም ባድማ [ናት]።
am.B: አገራችሁ ፈርሳለች፤ \q ከተሞቻችሁ በእሳት ተቃጥለዋል፤ \q እያያችሁ ባዕዳን እርሻችሁን ይበሉታል፤ \q ባዕዳን እንዳፈረሱት አገር ባድማ ሆናለች።
am.R: አገራችሁ ጠፍታለች። ከተሞቻችሁ ተቃጥለዋል። \q እናንተ እያያችሁ ባዕዳን የእርሻችሁን ሰብል ይወስዳሉ። \q የጠላት ሠራዊት አገርን እንደሚያፈርስ ሁሉም ነገር ወድሟል።

hi.L: तुम्हारा देश उजाड़ [है]; \q तुम्हारे नगर आग से जले हुए [हैं]; \q तुम्हारी भूमि: तुम्हारे सामने पराए लोग उसे खा रहे हैं, \q और [वह] उजाड़ [है], जैसे पराए लोगों का किया हुआ विनाश।
hi.B: तुम्हारा देश उजड़ा पड़ा है, \q तुम्हारे नगर जलकर राख हो गए हैं; \q तुम्हारे देखते-देखते विदेशी तुम्हारे खेत खा जाते हैं, \q और वह ऐसा उजड़ गया है जैसे विदेशियों ने उसे ढा दिया हो।
hi.R: तुम्हारा देश बरबाद हो गया है। तुम्हारे नगर जला दिए गए हैं। \q तुम्हारे देखते-देखते विदेशी तुम्हारे खेतों की फ़सल ले जा रहे हैं। \q सब कुछ नष्ट हो गया है, जैसे कोई शत्रु सेना किसी देश को उजाड़ देती है।

ru.L: Ваша земля — опустошение; \q ваши города сожжены огнём; \q вашу почву — у вас на глазах чужие пожирают её, \q и [она] — опустошение, как разрушение чужими.
ru.B: Ваша страна лежит в развалинах, \q ваши города сожжены; \q чужеземцы поедают ваши поля у вас на глазах, \q и всё опустошено, как земля, которую разорили чужеземцы.
ru.R: Ваша страна разорена. Ваши города сожжены. \q Чужеземцы забирают урожай с ваших полей, а вы только смотрите. \q Всё разрушено, как бывает, когда вражеское войско разоряет страну.

ja.L: あなたがたの地は荒れ果て、 \q あなたがたの町々は火で焼かれている。 \q あなたがたの土地は、あなたがたの目の前で、よそ者たちがそれを食い尽くしている。 \q [それは]よそ者に覆された所のように荒れ果てている。
ja.B: あなたがたの国は荒れ果て、 \q 町々は焼き払われた。 \q 畑の作物は、あなたがたが見ている前で、外国人が食い尽くし、 \q 外国人に打ち倒された地のように荒れ果てている。
ja.R: あなたたちの国は荒らされた。町々は焼かれてしまった。 \q あなたたちが見ている前で、外国人が畑の作物を奪っていく。 \q すべてが壊された。敵の軍隊が国をめちゃくちゃにしたときのようだ。

decisions.choice: land desolate, cities burned: an invasion of Judah
decisions.reason: The verse describes Judah overrun by a foreign army. It fits the Assyrian invasion of 701 BC, when Sennacherib took the fortified cities of Judah (36:1) and Jerusalem alone was left standing (verse 8), though an earlier invasion is possible (2 Chronicles 28:5-18).

decisions.choice: devouring: eating up the produce
decisions.reason: The strangers "eat" the ground: they take its harvest for themselves (Deuteronomy 28:33, 51).

decisions.choice: the received text: the overthrow of strangers
decisions.reason: "Overthrow" is the word used of the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah (Deuteronomy 29:22; Amos 4:11; Isaiah 13:19), and Sodom is named in verses 9 and 10. So the text could be corrected to "like the overthrow of Sodom". But the Hebrew text has "strangers", repeating the word from earlier in the verse, and that is followed here.

decisions.choice: taking the crops ... an enemy army
decisions.reason: Readable explains "devouring" as taking the crops and "strangers" who overthrow as an enemy army.

decisions.choice: पराए लोग (L); विदेशी (B)
decisions.reason: zarim are outsiders who do not belong to the land. पराए लोग keeps the Literal word "strangers"; Balanced says विदेशी, the word the Ezra pass uses for nokhri. परदेशी is kept for ger, the resident alien.

source.text: וְנוֹתְרָ֥ה בַת־צִיּ֖וֹן כְּסֻכָּ֣ה בְכָ֑רֶם כִּמְלוּנָ֥ה בְמִקְשָׁ֖ה כְּעִ֥יר נְצוּרָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And is left [the] daughter of Zion like a booth in a vineyard, like a hut in a cucumber field, like a city besieged.

en.L: And the daughter of Zion is left like a booth in a vineyard, \q like a hut in a cucumber field, like a besieged city.
en.B: Daughter Zion is left like a shelter among the vines, \q like a hut in a cucumber patch, like a town shut in by siege.
en.R: The people of Zion are left all alone. They are like a small shelter for a watchman in a vineyard, \q or a hut in a cucumber field. They are like a city with enemies all around it.

es.L: Y ha quedado la hija de Sion como una enramada en una viña, \q como una choza en un campo de pepinos, como una ciudad sitiada.
es.B: La hija de Sion ha quedado como un cobertizo entre las vides, \q como una choza en un pepinar, como una ciudad cercada por el enemigo.
es.R: El pueblo de Sion ha quedado completamente solo. Es como un pequeño refugio para un vigilante en una viña, \q o como una choza en un campo de pepinos. Es como una ciudad rodeada de enemigos.

fr.L: Et la fille de Sion est restée comme une cabane dans une vigne, \q comme une hutte dans un champ de concombres, comme une ville assiégée.
fr.B: La fille de Sion est restée comme un abri au milieu des vignes, \q comme une hutte dans un champ de concombres, comme une ville cernée par l’ennemi.
fr.R: Le peuple de Sion est resté tout seul. Il est comme le petit abri d’un gardien dans une vigne, \q ou comme une hutte dans un champ de concombres. Il est comme une ville entourée d’ennemis.

sw.L: Naye binti Sayuni ameachwa kama kibanda katika shamba la mizabibu, \q kama kibanda katika shamba la matango, kama mji uliozingirwa.
sw.B: Binti Sayuni ameachwa kama kibanda katikati ya mizabibu, \q kama kibanda katika shamba la matango, kama mji uliozungukwa na adui.
sw.R: Watu wa Sayuni wameachwa peke yao. Wako kama kibanda kidogo cha mlinzi katika shamba la mizabibu, \q au kibanda katika shamba la matango. Wako kama mji uliozungukwa na maadui pande zote.

vi.L: Và con gái Si-ôn bị bỏ lại như một chòi trong vườn nho, \q như một túp lều trong ruộng dưa, như một thành bị vây hãm.
vi.B: Con gái Si-ôn bị bỏ lại như cái chòi giữa vườn nho, \q như túp lều trong ruộng dưa, như một thành bị vây chặt.
vi.R: Dân Si-ôn bị bỏ lại trơ trọi. Họ giống như cái chòi nhỏ của người canh vườn nho, \q hay túp lều giữa ruộng dưa. Họ giống như một thành bị quân thù vây quanh.

ko.L: 그리고 딸 시온이 포도원의 초막같이, \q 오이밭의 원두막같이, 포위된 성읍같이 남았다.
ko.B: 딸 시온만 홀로 남았다. 포도밭의 초막 같고, \q 오이밭의 원두막 같고, 포위당한 성읍 같다.
ko.R: 시온 백성은 홀로 남았다. 그들은 포도밭을 지키는 사람이 머무는 작은 초막 같다. \q 오이밭의 원두막 같다. 적에게 둘러싸인 성읍 같다.

pt.L: E a filha de Sião é deixada como uma cabana numa vinha, \q como uma choça num campo de pepinos, como uma cidade sitiada.
pt.B: A filha de Sião ficou como um abrigo no meio das videiras, \q como uma choupana numa plantação de pepinos, como uma cidade cercada pelo inimigo.
pt.R: O povo de Sião ficou sozinho. É como uma pequena cabana de vigia numa plantação de uvas, \q ou uma choupana num campo de pepinos. É como uma cidade cercada de inimigos por todos os lados.

am.L: የጽዮንም ልጅ በወይን ቦታ እንዳለ ዳስ ቀረች፤ \q በዱባ እርሻ እንዳለ ጎጆ፣ እንደ ተከበበች ከተማ።
am.B: ልጅቷ ጽዮን በወይን ተክሎች መካከል እንዳለ መጠለያ ቀረች፤ \q በዱባ እርሻ እንዳለ ጎጆ፣ በጠላት እንደ ተከበበች ከተማ።
am.R: የጽዮን ሕዝብ ብቻቸውን ቀርተዋል። በወይን ቦታ ውስጥ ለጠባቂ እንደ ተሠራች ትንሽ ዳስ ሆነዋል፤ \q ወይም በዱባ እርሻ እንዳለች ጎጆ። ጠላቶች ዙሪያዋን እንደ ከበቧት ከተማ ሆነዋል።

hi.L: और सिय्योन की बेटी दाख की बारी में एक झोपड़ी के समान, \q ककड़ी के खेत में एक मचान के समान, घेरे हुए नगर के समान छोड़ दी गई है।
hi.B: सिय्योन की बेटी दाख की बारी में एक छप्पर के समान छोड़ दी गई है, \q ककड़ी की बाड़ी में एक मचान के समान, घेराबंदी में फँसे नगर के समान।
hi.R: सिय्योन के लोग बिलकुल अकेले छोड़ दिए गए हैं। वे अंगूर के बाग़ में रखवाले की छोटी-सी झोपड़ी के समान हैं, \q या ककड़ी के खेत में बनी एक मचान के समान। वे उस नगर के समान हैं जिसे शत्रुओं ने चारों ओर से घेर लिया हो।

ru.L: И оставлена дочь Сиона, как шалаш в винограднике, \q как сторожка на огуречном поле, как осаждённый город.
ru.B: Дочь Сиона осталась, как навес среди лоз, \q как шалаш на огуречной грядке, как город в кольце осады.
ru.R: Жители Сиона остались совсем одни. Они как маленький шалаш сторожа в винограднике \q или как хижина на огуречном поле. Они как город, окружённый врагами.

ja.L: そして娘シオンは残された、ぶどう畑の仮小屋のように、 \q きゅうり畑の番小屋のように、包囲された町のように。
ja.B: 娘シオンは取り残された、ぶどう畑の中の仮小屋のように、 \q きゅうり畑の番小屋のように、敵に囲まれた町のように。
ja.R: シオンの人々は、ぽつんと取り残された。ぶどう畑で見張りをする人の小さな小屋のようだ。 \q きゅうり畑の小屋のようだ。敵に周りを囲まれた町のようだ。

decisions.choice: daughter of Zion: Jerusalem and its people, pictured as a young woman
decisions.reason: Zion is the hill of Jerusalem and stands for the city. "Daughter Zion" pictures the city and its people as a young woman, loved and vulnerable (10:32; 37:22; Lamentations 2:13).

decisions.choice: a booth in a vineyard, a hut in a cucumber field: a flimsy shelter standing alone
decisions.reason: Watchmen built rough shelters of branches to guard the crops while they ripened (Job 27:18). Such a hut stood alone in the field, small and easily blown down (24:20). Jerusalem stands by itself in a ruined land.

decisions.choice: besieged: shut in by an enemy
decisions.reason: The form most likely means "besieged". It could also be read from the verb "to watch": a guarded or watched city. Either way the city is hemmed in.

decisions.choice: the people of Zion ... a small shelter for a watchman
decisions.reason: Readable says "the people of Zion" for "the daughter of Zion" and explains who used the shelter.

decisions.choice: la hija de Sion (L, B); el pueblo de Sion (R)
decisions.reason: As Matthew 21:5 and John 12:15, L and B keep "la hija de Sion" and R says who is meant, "el pueblo de Sion", as the English R does. Book-wide choice, recorded once for chapters 1-20.

decisions.choice: "binti Sayuni" (L), "Binti Sayuni" (B), "watu wa Sayuni" (R)
decisions.reason: The settled form for Isaiah, as 2 Kings 19:21; Readable says who is meant, as the English Readable does (m1).

decisions.choice: "la fille de Sion" (L, B); "le peuple de Sion" (R)
decisions.reason: As 2 Kings 19:21; Readable names the people, as the English Readable does. For the whole book.

decisions.choice: "con gái Si-ôn" (L, B); "dân Si-ôn" (R)
decisions.reason: The terms note's form, as 2 Kings 19:21; Readable says who is meant, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "딸 시온" (L, B); "시온 백성" (R)
decisions.reason: The terms note's forms, as 2 Kings 19:21 (= Isaiah 37:22).

decisions.choice: a filha de Sião (L, B); o povo de Sião (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: the picture of the city and its people as a young woman (m1) is "a filha de Sião" at Literal and Balanced, the usual Portuguese form; "Filha Sião" without the preposition, as the English Balanced says "Daughter Zion", is not natural Portuguese. Readable says "o povo de Sião", as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: daughter of Zion: "የጽዮን ልጅ" (L), "ልጅቱ ጽዮን" (B), "የጽዮን ሕዝብ" (R)
decisions.reason: The terms list keeps the Hebrew figure at Literal and follows the English wording at Balanced ("Daughter Zion") and Readable ("the people of Zion"). "ልጅቱ" makes plain that the city itself is pictured as the daughter.

decisions.choice: सिय्योन की बेटी
decisions.reason: "Daughter Zion" is सिय्योन की बेटी, the form the terms note fixes for the Prophets; Readable says सिय्योन के लोग, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: मचान
decisions.reason: The melunah was a watchman's lodge on poles in a field; मचान is the raised hut Indian farmers still build to watch their crops, and keeps it apart from the booth (झोपड़ी, छप्पर) in the vineyard.

decisions.choice: "дочь Сиона"
decisions.reason: The Prophets note settles one form for "daughter Zion" through these books: "дочь Сиона", modern Russian rather than the Slavonic "дщерь Сионова". Readable, as the English, names the people of the city.

decisions.choice: bat Tsiyyon "daughter Zion": "娘シオン" (L, B), as Lamentations and 2 Kings 19:21; Readable follows the English Readable ("シオンの人々"). The city is never "彼女". Zion alone is "シオン", har Tsiyyon "シオンの山".
decisions.reason: The appositional form "娘シオン" says that Zion herself is the daughter (m1), not a daughter belonging to Zion, and keeps one form across Isaiah, Lamentations and the other prophets.

source.text: לוּלֵי֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת הוֹתִ֥יר לָ֛נוּ שָׂרִ֖יד כִּמְעָ֑ט כִּסְדֹ֣ם הָיִ֔ינוּ לַעֲמֹרָ֖ה דָּמִֽינוּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: If not Yahweh of hosts had left to us survivors a few, like Sodom we would have been, Gomorrah we would have resembled.

en.L: If {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts had not left us survivors, a few, \q we would have been like Sodom, \q we would have resembled Gomorrah.
en.B: Had {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies not let a few of us survive, \q we would have shared the fate of Sodom; \q Gomorrah's end would have been ours.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies let a few of us live. \q If {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had not, we would have been wiped out like the city of Sodom. \q We would have been destroyed like Gomorrah.

es.L: Si {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos no nos hubiera dejado sobrevivientes, unos pocos, \q habríamos sido como Sodoma, \q nos habríamos parecido a Gomorra.
es.B: Si {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos no hubiera dejado con vida a unos pocos de nosotros, \q habríamos corrido la suerte de Sodoma; \q el fin de Gomorra habría sido el nuestro.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos dejó con vida a unos pocos de nosotros. \q Si no lo hubiera hecho, habríamos sido destruidos por completo, como la ciudad de Sodoma. \q Habríamos sido destruidos como Gomorra.

fr.L: Si {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées ne nous avait laissé des rescapés, un petit nombre, \q nous serions comme Sodome, \q nous ressemblerions à Gomorrhe.
fr.B: Si {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées n’avait pas laissé survivre quelques-uns d’entre nous, \q nous aurions eu le sort de Sodome ; \q la fin de Gomorrhe aurait été la nôtre.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées a laissé vivre quelques-uns d’entre nous. \q Sinon, nous aurions été anéantis comme la ville de Sodome. \q Nous aurions été détruits comme Gomorrhe.

sw.L: Kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi asingalituachia waliookoka, wachache, \q tungalikuwa kama Sodoma, \q tungalifanana na Gomora.
sw.B: Kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi asingaliwaacha wachache wetu waokoke, \q tungalipatwa na yaliyoipata Sodoma; \q mwisho wa Gomora ungalikuwa wetu.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi aliwaacha wachache wetu waishi. \q Kama asingalifanya hivyo, tungalifutiliwa mbali kama mji wa Sodoma. \q Tungaliangamizwa kama Gomora.

vi.L: Nếu {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân không để lại cho chúng ta những người sống sót, một số ít, \q thì chúng ta đã như Sô-đôm, \q chúng ta đã giống Gô-mô-rơ.
vi.B: Nếu {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân không chừa lại cho chúng ta một ít người sống sót, \q thì chúng ta đã chịu chung số phận với Sô-đôm, \q và cùng một kết cục như Gô-mô-rơ.
vi.R: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân đã để cho một ít người trong chúng ta được sống. \q Nếu {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không làm vậy, chúng ta đã bị xóa sạch như thành Sô-đôm. \q Chúng ta đã bị hủy diệt như Gô-mô-rơ.

ko.L: 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 우리에게 생존자를 조금 남겨 두지 않으셨다면, \q 우리는 소돔같이 되었을 것이고, \q 고모라와 같아졌을 것이다.
ko.B: 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 우리 가운데 몇 사람이라도 살려 두지 않으셨다면, \q 우리는 소돔처럼 멸망하고, \q 고모라와 같은 꼴이 되었을 것이다.
ko.R: 하늘의 군대를 거느리신 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 우리 가운데 몇 사람을 살려 두셨다. \q 그렇게 하지 않으셨다면 우리는 소돔 성처럼 완전히 없어졌을 것이다. \q 고모라처럼 멸망했을 것이다.

pt.L: Se {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos não nos tivesse deixado sobreviventes, uns poucos, \q seríamos como Sodoma, \q seríamos semelhantes a Gomorra.
pt.B: Se {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos não tivesse deixado que alguns de nós sobrevivessem, \q teríamos tido o destino de Sodoma; \q o fim de Gomorra teria sido o nosso.
pt.R: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos deixou alguns de nós com vida. \q Se {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} não tivesse feito isso, teríamos sido destruídos como a cidade de Sodoma. \q Teríamos acabado como Gomorra.

am.L: {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ጸባኦት ጥቂት ትሩፋን ባያስቀርልን ኖሮ፣ \q እንደ ሰዶም በሆንን ነበር፤ \q ገሞራንም በመሰልን ነበር።
am.B: የሠራዊት አምላክ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ከእኛ ጥቂቶች እንዲተርፉ ባያደርግ ኖሮ፣ \q የሰዶም ዕጣ በደረሰብን ነበር፤ \q የገሞራም መጨረሻ የእኛ በሆነ ነበር።
am.R: የሠራዊት አምላክ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ከእኛ ጥቂቶቻችን በሕይወት እንድንኖር አደረገ። \q እንዲህ ባያደርግ ኖሮ እንደ ሰዶም ከተማ ፈጽመን በጠፋን ነበር። \q እንደ ገሞራም በወደምን ነበር።

hi.L: यदि सेनाओं के {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} ने हमारे लिए कुछ थोड़े-से बचे हुए न छोड़े होते, \q तो हम सदोम के समान हो जाते, \q [और] अमोरा के तुल्य ठहरते।
hi.B: यदि सेनाओं के {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} ने हममें से थोड़े लोगों को बचा न रखा होता, \q तो हम सदोम के समान हो जाते, \q और अमोरा के जैसे बन जाते।
hi.R: सेनाओं के {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} ने हममें से कुछ लोगों को जीवित रहने दिया। \q यदि वे ऐसा न करते, तो हम सदोम नगर की तरह पूरी तरह मिट गए होते। \q हम अमोरा की तरह नष्ट हो गए होते।

ru.L: Если бы {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}} Саваоф не оставил нам уцелевших, немногих, \q мы стали бы как Содом, \q уподобились бы Гоморре.
ru.B: Если бы {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}} Саваоф не сохранил немногих из нас, \q мы стали бы как Содом, \q мы были бы как Гоморра.
ru.R: {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}} Воинств оставил в живых немногих из нас. \q Если бы {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} этого не сделал, мы были бы стёрты с лица земли, как город Содом. \q Мы погибли бы, как Гоморра.

ja.L: もし万軍の{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}が、わずかな生き残りをわたしたちに残してくださらなかったなら、 \q わたしたちはソドムのようになり、 \q ゴモラに似たものとなっていただろう。
ja.B: 万軍の{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}が、わたしたちのうちわずかな者を生き残らせてくださらなかったなら、 \q わたしたちはソドムと同じ運命をたどり、 \q ゴモラと同じ最期を迎えていただろう。
